quarterly_data.signal: CFO Moshe Eisenberg on Q1 2026 (non-GAAP): gross profit $62 million; gross margin 51%, similar to the previous quarter - 'I expect the gross margin to improve in the second half of the year', on the revenue forecast and the contribution of Hawk and Eagle G5. Operating expenses $30.9 million versus $24.4 million in Q1 2025 and $28.7 million in Q4 2025, increasing mainly in R&D and sales and marketing to support the expected growth, and on the weaker US dollar against the shekel. Financial income $8.1 million; net income $35.3 million versus $38.7 million a year earlier. Cash, deposits and marketable securities $850 million at March 31, 2026. Inventory optimized to $116.7 million, expected to increase in the coming quarters; receivables rose to $131.7 million from $90.8 million on collection timing, lowering cash generation. COO Ramy Langer: 'there is some pressure from the supply chain, but at the same time we continue to implement cost reduction in our machine', with gross margin improving in the second half.
quarterly_data.figure: gross profit $62 million; opex $30.9 million; net income $35.3 million; inventory $116.7 million; cash $850 million

quarterly_data.signal: COO Ramy Langer on the cycle: Camtek's advanced-packaging segment tends 'to lag behind the front end by, I would say, 1 or 2 quarters'; 'the AI is the engine, is the fuel, what's fueling the entire industry and our business as well', while other applications grow in parallel, including the OSAT business, and across regions - 'the market is starting to ramp'. Growth starts to show already in Q2 and 'we expect that this growth will continue into 2027.' On 2026 growth versus peers: 'If the question suggests that we are losing market share, the answer is absolutely no' - 2026 is measured against record 2025 revenue, and for the first half of 2027 'the growth will be very, very significant'. Supply: Camtek has enough inventory and is ramping it to respond; for the $260 million of HBM orders and forecast, 'from supply chain capabilities, we have no issues.'

COO Ramy Langer on markets: 'today our inspection business is to about two-thirds of our overall business'; Camtek's addressable market today is 'above $1.5 billion, $1.7 billion', growing by about $0.5 billion, with targeted inspection applications including the back end of the front-end line, compound semiconductors, CMOS image sensors and RF. Photonics: 'definitely we are involved there', but 'the magnitude of the business is smaller compared with the larger applications.' China: pressure at the lower-end applications, mainly from local players and also from foreign players; Camtek's large installed base and the OSAT build-up in China support the business - 'I expect that we will see a positive trend in the foreseeable future in China.' AI software (CEO Rafi Amit): first, software packages with the AI capability for the thousands of systems in Camtek's installed base; second phase, Visual Layer solutions for the wider semiconductor industry. COO: the AI inspection and metrology capabilities are to be introduced to customers 'in the very next few month'.
quarterly_data.figure: inspection about two-thirds of business; addressable market today above $1.5 billion, $1.7 billion
